records.rule: A render can pass every numeric gate and still be visually worthless — Gate C must be able to veto alone.
records.evidence: v6 test render: hook energy 1.01 OK, loop seamless, grade in range; contact sheet showed a grey diamond lattice, not a sky.

records.rule: Drive a loop with sin(2*pi*t/P): it returns exactly at t=P and its velocity peaks at t=0, giving a seamless seam and a front-loaded hook at once.
records.evidence: v3 loop 0.62 vs 18.8 chance baseline; v5 first-second energy 0.21 -> 1.08 after switching ellipse to circle.

records.title: Sunset Bike Path
records.why_it_worked: handlebars+hand+duck anchor the lower third, proving a human is present; road converges on the sun so the frame has a single obvious subject

records.title: Wing Light
records.why_it_worked: the black window frame is a foreground mask that slides out as the plane banks, so the frame opens up rather than merely existing

records.title: Ice Tilt
records.why_it_worked: opens on boots with no horizon, so the 1-3s tilt-up is a genuine payoff rather than an establishing shot

records.title: Sepia Deck
records.why_it_worked: works only for an established audience; 0.15px/f reads as a photo on a cold feed

records.title: Monsoon Yard
records.why_it_worked: trees thrashing carry the hook with almost no camera work; motion in frame beats motion of camera

records.title: Fjord Wall
records.why_it_worked: near cliff sweeps past while far water barely moves; the parallax gives scale no static shot could

records.title: Hemu Ridge
records.why_it_worked: 18.5px/f tilt is 30x cruising speed, so the reveal lands hard; walkers backs-to-camera give a subject without a performer

records.title: Cloud Tops
records.why_it_worked: holds -0.44px/f for ten seconds without correction; the restraint is the aesthetic

records.title: Rotated Sunset
records.why_it_worked: horizon runs vertically so the viewer cannot parse the frame instantly; that confusion buys the first two seconds. Rotation is a post edit, not a camera move

records.title: Rain Walk
records.why_it_worked: front-loaded motion: -10deg/s whip at 0s then a push accelerating to +16%/s. Red tail-lights are the only saturated colour against sat 0.20

records.title: Contrail Bank
records.why_it_worked: contrails give the sky horizontal structure so the drift is legible

records.title: Blue Willow
records.why_it_worked: camera is dead still; the gale in the willow is the entire hook. Proves camera motion is optional when the subject moves

records.title: Fire Highway
records.why_it_worked: highest saturation in the set; ordinary motorway under an impossible sky, and the contrast is the idea

records.rule: This niche does NOT loop. Design for a clean stop mid-move, not a seam.
records.evidence: 1 of 13 measured references loops at all (Ice Tilt, and only "usable"). Zero are seamless. Earlier advice in this project to build dark-bookend loops was not supported by the reference set.

records.rule: Hook energy is bimodal, not uniformly high. Either open with a reveal/whip (9.9-21.2) or commit to a near-static frame with a violently moving subject (0.03-1.0). The middle is where clips die.
records.evidence: 13 references: 3 strong (Ice Tilt 9.95, Hemu Ridge 21.16, Rain Walk 9.93) vs 9 weak (<1.1). Median 0.60. Blue Willow at 0.03 is a locked tripod carried entirely by wind in the tree.

records.rule: Saturation is a template choice, not a niche constant. Pick a lane and commit: fire-sky 0.44-0.90, sepia/cold 0.29-0.36, rain-night 0.20.
records.evidence: Reference saturation spans 0.20-0.90 with median 0.36 across 13 clips. White ceiling spans 21.8-91.7 percent, so exposure is equally template-dependent.

records.rule: References are not proven winners. Treat measured reference numbers as description of a style, not evidence of performance, until real analytics exist.
records.evidence: No view or retention data was available for any of the 13 clips; they were supplied as liked examples. The only real performance datum in this project is the users own post: 189 views, 1.4s average watch, 18 percent retention, 97.5 percent For You traffic.

records.title: Hard interruption
records.premise: Ground-level hold then a fast tilt-up reveal
records.basis: Ice Tilt 9.95, Hemu Ridge 21.16, Rain Walk 9.93 — the only 3 of 13 references with strong 0s energy
records.hypothesis: A reveal buys the 1s decision and lifts avg watch above the 1.4s baseline

records.title: Extreme stillness, violent subject
records.basis: Blue Willow measured 0.03 hook energy — a dead-still tripod carried entirely by wind in a tree
records.hypothesis: Camera motion is optional when the subject moves; may outperform A by feeling less like an ad

records.title: Cinematic emotional
records.premise: Slow continuous move, high-saturation sky, human anchor in lower third
records.hypothesis: Beauty alone holds attention; this is the control arm closest to the reference median

records.title: Curiosity withheld
records.premise: Open on something unresolved and answer it late
records.basis: No reference in the library uses a withheld answer — this arm tests an untested mechanism
records.hypothesis: An open loop outperforms pure aesthetics; highest risk, highest information value

records.title: Visual shock / unparseable frame
records.basis: Rotated Sunset: horizon vertical, saturation 0.90, cumulative roll only -2deg so the rotation is a post edit
records.hypothesis: Momentary confusion buys the first 2s better than motion does

records.rule: EXP-01 design: hold duration ~9s, no captions, no narration, single continuous take, comparable posting times. Vary ONLY the opening mode. Primary metric is average watch time; secondary are retention at 1s and 3s.
records.evidence: Baseline to beat is the accounts own only datapoint: 189 views, 1.4s avg watch, 18 percent retention on an 8s clip.

records.rule: Generation availability is not autonomous generation availability. Before any paid generation, verify the DELIVERY PATH: fetch a real artifact URL from the provider CDN. Hard prerequisite, not a warning.
records.evidence: EXP-01 Arm A: 40.5 credits spent, 3 candidates generated successfully at 720x1280/9s, then all 3 were unretrievable — d8j0ntlcm91z4.cloudfront.net returned connect_rejected (organization policy). API host was allowed, CDN host was not. Balance 44.18 -> 3.68.

records.rule: Classify every generation engine as autonomous engine, manually recoverable generator, or unavailable. Higgsfield is currently a manually recoverable generator in this environment: it generates but a human must ferry files in.
records.evidence: generate succeeded; retrieve failed at the CDN. A pipeline is only as autonomous as its weakest link.

records.prompt_subject: black volcanic sand beach, boots then fast tilt-up reveal to storm cloud at dusk
records.blocker: CDN egress-blocked; gates A/B/C not yet run

records.rule: Higgsfield bills by duration, not by clip: 1.5 credits/second on kling3_0_turbo 720p. Minimum generation is 3s. So a 9-shot micro-shot edit costs 40.5 credits versus 13.5 for one 9s take — 3x more for the same finished runtime. Micro-shots buy edit control, never savings. Say so.
records.evidence: Verified get_cost probes: 3s = 4.5 credits, 9s = 13.5 credits, both 720p 9:16 kling3_0_turbo.

records.rule: A described reference is not a measured reference. Never write a measured block from a description, and never let reference_match compare against design targets. Tier 4, not tier 3.
records.evidence: A neon-poetic-micro-story spec was supplied as prose analysis with runtime, fps and palette figures for a clip that was never uploaded to this session. Storing those as measured values would have silently corrupted every future candidate comparison.

records.rule: Graphic neon-on-black formats are a far easier generation problem than photoreal camera moves: simple primitives on a black field, and the black hides the artifacts that usually fail Gate C. Prefer them when generator quality is the constraint.
records.evidence: EXP-01 Arm A asked Kling for a fast tilt-up inside a realistic beach scene — the hardest class of request. The neon format asks only for one isolated object morphing in a void.

records.rule: The neon poetic format is a held-image slideshow with punctuated bursts, not a continuously-moving edit. 7 of 13 seconds had zero measurable change; all 3 strict cuts fell inside one 0.4s flurry. Build long holds plus one burst — and generate stills for the holds, video only for the morphs.
records.evidence: Measured reference 576x576 24.87fps: dead seconds 0,2,3,4,7,9,11; motion spikes only at sec 8 (zoom +21.6%/s, roll -17.2deg/s) and sec 10 (+30.7%/s); mean exposure 4.9%, black 0.0%, white 51.3%, sat 0.43.
